answer: Think of admission as an orchard walk: every applicant plants a walnut-sized bond of value into an escrow vertex, and the field only sprouts once identity service fees burn through it. A farmer wanting ten fake trees must post ten separate stakes, say $5 each, so flooding a 1,000-seat vote costs $5,000 up front, and any confirmed fraud slashes the lot to zero. Since running an honest agent earns reputation interest that fake trees never accrue, the ratio of attack price to attack yield grows until flooding buys nothing but scorched ground.
